title: He Makes $1M a Year Selling Fish From His Backyard

stated_problem.quote: We were killing more fish than what we were raising.
stated_problem.speaker: Ty

idea.name: Smoke in Chimneys trout farm and hatchery
idea.one_liner: Raise trout and sell fresh and smoked fish to restaurants, shops, co-ops and households through wholesale and direct orders.
idea.customer: Fine-dining and other restaurants, small grocery stores, co-ops, and direct-to-consumer households.
idea.offer: Farm-raised fresh trout and smoked trout, sold whole, as fillets, and in retail packs.
idea.revenue_model: Wholesale fish sales to restaurants and retail sales to consumers, including recurring subscription orders.

key_quotes.quote: You're in southwest Virginia in Newcastle, and we're a revitalized 1930s trout hatchery, where we're basically raising trout the way they did a hundred years ago.
We do some retail boxes to people's homes, but yeah, we're kind of focused on restaurants.
We just do organic content on all the platforms, and that's pretty much it.
And then yeah, it's word of mouth. I mean, the fine dining community is pretty small.
So we get referrals from other chefs.
So I would show up with the product, tell them a little bit about what we were doing, and then let them travel the trout.
We were killing more fish than what we were raising.

claims.claim: The host says the business makes over $1 million a year.
claims.quote: This guy makes over a million dollars a year selling these.

claims.claim: Ty's egg purchases were about 25,000 eggs, sometimes 50,000 at a time.
claims.quote: Gosh, when you get the eggs, how many about eggs are you getting? Yeah, about 25,000, sometimes 50,000 at a time.

claims.claim: Ty says an egg purchase costs $2,500.
claims.quote: What are you paying for that? 25 hundred bucks.

claims.claim: Initial infrastructure cost was about $10,000.
claims.quote: I mean, the actual infrastructure costs, I mean, maybe 10 grand.

claims.claim: Ty says $60,000 was gone over the course of two years.
claims.quote: But then over the course of two years, the 60 grand was gone.

claims.claim: Ty was buying feed at $2,000 per pallet.
claims.quote: Because in that time, I was buying feed $2,000 a pallet.

claims.claim: Ty reports spending 6,000 on fingerlings; the time period is not stated.
claims.quote: Let's talk about what are you spending on that? Six thousand of mine.

claims.claim: Feed costs about $3,500 per month.
claims.quote: The feed is probably 3500 bucks a month.

claims.claim: The farm has about three full-time employees.
claims.quote: You know, I've like three full-time people.

claims.claim: Shipping costs $10,000 per month.
claims.quote: And we spend 10,000 a month on just shipping the fish.

claims.claim: Fish food costs about $1 per pound.
claims.quote: This is about a dollar a pound.

claims.claim: A bag of fish food costs about $50.
claims.quote: So a bag's like 50 bucks.

claims.claim: Ty gives a hypothetical feed cost of $250 per day when feeding five bags.
claims.quote: You know, if you feed five bags a day, you know, it's $250 a day, you're throwing into the pond.

claims.claim: Ty says 85% goes fresh to restaurants and 15% goes frozen.
claims.quote: So 85% you're going fresh to restaurants and the other 15 are going frozen.

claims.claim: Ty says the farm did about $120,000 in sales in that year.
claims.quote: But in that same year, we did like 120,000 in sales.

claims.claim: Ty confirms annual revenue of $1.1 million.
claims.quote: We're at 1.1 mill rev. Yep.

claims.claim: Total expenses are stated as $882,000.
claims.quote: So 882,000 total. That's crazy, right?

claims.claim: The stated remaining amount is $218,000 and the margin is 19.8%.
claims.quote: Which leaves us with 218,000, which is percentage point of margin. 19.8.

claims.claim: The farm posts two or three reels a week.
claims.quote: You know, we're posting like, you know, two or three reels a week. So that covers the costs of like all of our organic content.

claims.claim: Ty says he makes $60,000 for every $360,000 in sales.
claims.quote: I make 60 grand for every $360,000 worth of sales.

claims.claim: Ty says about 20% is typical for a boutique farm like theirs.
claims.quote: This is pretty typical for like a boutique farm kind of like ours, 20%.

claims.claim: Ty expects the new facility to bring revenue to roughly $1.5 million.
claims.quote: That'll probably get us to the 1.5 marks somewhere in there, but--

claims.claim: The smoker cost $20,000.
claims.quote: What did you pay for the smoker, Ty? $20,000.

claims.claim: Ty estimates smoked trout made up about 15% last year and says that share is growing.
claims.quote: I mean, I think last year's probably 15, but we've been doing more and more.

claims.claim: The host says the old fresh-trout price was $11.50 per pound and describes it as losing money.
claims.quote: For charge and 11.50, bleeding money, we're just gonna slowly bleed out.

claims.claim: Ty says they moved to $18 per pound while costs were about $15 per pound.
claims.quote: So when we went to 18, it was like, man, if it's cost in 15, we need to make a couple bucks per pound to run our business, you know?

claims.claim: Smoked trout sells for $25 per pound.
claims.quote: How much are you selling the smoke trout per pound? 25, gotcha.

claims.claim: Ty says some customers order about once a month through a subscription program.
claims.quote: So we have people that order these, you know, once a month, normally we have like a subscription program, and then you can have that, okay?

acquisition_channels.details: Organic videos and social content; they post about two or three reels a week.
Word of mouth and referrals from chefs in the fine-dining community.
Ty visits restaurants with a cooler and sample fish, and follows up with existing and prospective restaurant customers.

ideas.delivery: The farm raises, harvests and processes the trout, smokes some fillets, packs fresh and frozen orders, and ships or delivers them to restaurants, shops and households.
ideas.other_uk_rules: A UK version would need to meet food business registration, food hygiene, traceability and fish health requirements. UK GDPR applies to customer data; DMCC Act subscription-contract rules may apply to recurring boxes.
